linkedin/carousel/slide-1.png: Slide 1: "The 11pm phone call every one of us knows." Why I built Parwah, by Anchit Tandon, founder.
linkedin/carousel/slide-2.png: Slide 2: "Sab theek hai, beta. And the call ends." You hear the words, not the week. So many of us live in one city while our parents live in another.
linkedin/carousel/slide-3.png: Slide 3: Caring for parents is a group project with no real place to do it. The doctor's number in one phone, papers in a drawer, one tired sibling, a noisy family group.
linkedin/carousel/slide-4.png: Slide 4: "One family app. Parents in charge." The family's Parwah Today screen.
linkedin/carousel/slide-5.png: Slide 5: "Three big buttons. Nothing else to learn." Papa's screen with SOS, All is well and Medicines taken.
linkedin/carousel/slide-6.png: Slide 6: "Together, with their yes." Parents switch on location themselves, joining needs a yes, ID papers keep only the last 4 digits, free scam check. Reassurance, never surveillance.
linkedin/carousel/slide-7.png: Slide 7: "Set it up together this Diwali." Free for families. Link in the first comment.
whatsapp/status-diwali-1080x1920.png: Diwali WhatsApp Status with a glowing diya: "Ghar ki safai ho gayi? Ab family ke papers bhi." Doctors, medicines, insurance and the emergency card in one free family app, Parwah.
